messages:
sylvia: Heads up — EU canary is showing massive slowdowns when rendering choropleth on /customers/map. Local builds are fine.
ryan: Saw this too around 21:12 UTC. Paint goes from ~120ms -> ~1.2s. Main thread dominated by parse + render.
maggie: Took a quick profiler dump. The new telemetry change added `topojson-client` into the same chunk as telemetry-proxy; chunk grew ~120KB and parsing shows up in the flamegraph. Also doubled up a telemetry import so modules parse twice.
leo: That telemetry-sidecar canary rollout went at ~21:10 per deploy-bot. Could be correlated.
deploy-bot: deploy: telemetry-proxy v3.4.2 -> canary started at 2025-07-01T21:10:12Z; status: success
ryan: Minimal flame trace:
```
main
 ├─ parseChunk (telemetry-proxy.bundle.js)
 ├─ renderChoropleth
 └─ drawPaths
```
sylvia: We're also seeing KV-prefetch churn — multiple widgets request the same topojson blob concurrently which causes duplicate fetches and eviction. Prefetch hitrate on canary dropped to ~18%.
maggie: That matches the client prefetch policy change in the telemetry PR — prefetch switched to `eager`. With high concurrency, eager causes duplicate chunk downloads across isolates.
leo: Quick non-code mitigation: inject header `x-prefetch-policy: conservative` on the canary route via routing override so we don't need a rollback.
ryan: Conservative will increase cold load latency a bit for some flows but avoids the main-thread parse explosion. It's a routing-level tradeoff.
maggie: Ran a staging run with conservative prefetch header and the paint times went down to ~150ms. I'll open a tiny PR to add the canary header override and a reorder of telemetry imports to reduce chunk coupling.
sylvia: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/7891 — adds canary routing override and a small change to import ordering to avoid duplicate module parse.
leo: We should add a telemetry metric `client.chunk.parse_ms` (per-chunk parse time) — current metrics only show aggregate parse and obscure which chunk is the culprit.
maggie: Added the metric and created a dashboard tile (p50/p95) in the PR. Will ship together with the override so we can monitor impact in real time.
ryan: If this doesn't fix it, what's rollback plan?
sylvia: Plan A: switch canary routing back to previous telemetry-proxy revision (instant via routing). Plan B: remove eager prefetch header and ship client change/rollback. I'll flip Plan A if user-visible LCP regressions continue.
deploy-bot: alert: canary frontend LCP p95 spiked; error rate up 0.8%; notifying #incidents
sylvia: I'm flipping the canary routing back to the prior telemetry-proxy revision now and watching metrics. Will report when stable. :eyes:
